title: Brain Tumour Detection Using EfficientNet-Transformer Hybrid Network with SHAP and Grad-CAM Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence
content: Accurate and interpretable brain tumour detection from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains a significant challenge in computer-aided diagnosis. This study proposes an EfficientNet–Transformer Hybrid Network integrated with SHapley Additive ExPlanations (SHAP) and Grad-CAM explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques for automated and trustworthy brain tumour classification. Methods: The proposed framework combines EfficientNet for local feature extraction and a Vision Transformer for global contextual learning. MRI images from publicly available benchmark datasets containing four classes (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumour, and no tumour) were preprocessed and augmented before training. The model was trained using an 80:20 training-testing split, while SHAP and Grad-CAM were employed to provide feature-level and spatial explanations of predictions. Results: The proposed framework achieved a classification accuracy of 98.88%, outperforming several state-of-the-art CNN and transformer models. It also attained average precision, recall, and F1-score values of 98.90%, 98.88%, and 98.89%, respectively, with an average AUC of 0.9893. Ablation and robustness analyses demonstrated that integrating SHAP and Grad-CAM improved interpretability while maintaining high predictive performance under noisy conditions. Conclusions: The proposed EfficientNet–Transformer framework effectively combines local and global feature learning with dual explainability mechanisms to deliver accurate and clinically interpretable brain tumour classification. The results demonstrate its potential as a reliable computer-aided diagnosis tool for neuro-oncology and clinical decision support systems.
